subject: bat
reasoning:
I'm planning out a compact bat model with the SDK, thinking through realistic proportions—small body around 7cm with a 0.3-0.4m wingspan—and considering how to pose it so it stands properly on the ground rather than in a hanging or flying position.

I'm working out the joint hierarchy in meters: hips as root, a short spine chain running from hips to chest, then a neck and head joint, with the whole skeleton parented and positioned to keep the lowest points touching the floor.

Then I'm sweeping a tapered body mesh along the spine path with varying radii for a rounded, mottled brown torso, and starting to build a sphere-based head shape attached to the head bone.

Now I'm shaping the snout, upper and lower jaws, and extruding triangular ear outlines on each side of the head with sharp tips.

Laying out the wing skeleton...

Working out the leg segments from hip to foot with lengths that sum to just enough reach, and choosing a bend hint so the knee angles backward-out like a real bat's. Using a two-segment limb that returns hip, knee, and ankle joint names so the foot lands as the tip point.

For toes, I'm spiking three small points off the foot joint angled slightly downward and forward so they just graze the floor without sinking too deep, keeping the offset well within the acceptable margin relative to overall body height.

Shifting the root position seems fragile, so I'll skip that and instead focus on the thumb claws pointing forward-up from the wrist rather than downward. I'm setting up the wing arm chain as a three-point polyline from shoulder to elbow to wrist, parented to the spine, with named joints for each segment.

For the fingers, I'm defining four digit chains per wing, each a three-point polyline from wrist to a mid-joint to tip, parented off the arm's wrist tip, with slight droop added at the midpoint to avoid perfectly straight segments. Each finger gets its own tapered sweep radius.

Now I'm adding membranes between adjacent fingers (f2-f3, f3-f4, f4-f5) as paired-edge chains running root to tip, and working out the plagiopatagium membrane connecting the fifth finger back to the arm and body flank, bounded by the shoulder-elbow-wrist edge on one side and the wrist-to-tip finger edge on the other.

Still writing membrane geometry...

I'll mirror the membrane as a simple two-edge quad from hip to ankle and tailbase to tailtip on each side, keeping points close to the floor since low heights there are fine. For the bone bindings, I need to explicitly specify which bone each point-array edge should follow since they don't have their own chain.

Still defining membrane materials...

Building the tail membrane shape...

Shaping the head and muzzle now, flattening the skull and tapering a frustum muzzle from it, keeping everything parented to the head bone for the fur-colored geometry.

Placing the fangs near the jaw bottom, then adding a dark nose sphere at the muzzle tip and small black eye spheres with highlights on the head bone. I'm also thickening the ears and giving them a thin pink inner layer via a second smaller extrude.

I'm setting up the skeleton hierarchy now: spine joints leading to a neck joint, then the head joint parented off the neck, following the "left/forward/up" local coordinate convention for the model's own left side.

I'll fix the neck endpoint and apply a mottled fur paint with countershading on the belly for the body and head parts, reusing it on sphere elements too. For fingers, the chain can parent off the arm's tip joint, and I'm setting up the finger tip positions next.

Working out midpoint helper and arm joint coordinates for shoulder, elbow, and wrist, then mirroring sides with an L/R label before handling membrane orientation...

For legs, I'm sweeping the geometry for the leg and foot, setting up the limb joint points with hip and foot positions, lengths, and a bend-direction hint for the knee, then building the leg chain from the array of points.

I'm checking the reach distance from hip to foot stays within limb length limits, then listing out the color palette: fur tones, belly, wing membrane, skin, dark, claw, and white, and starting to set up the mottled wing membrane coloring.
